children: shares rose 2.63% at 10.30 a.m. ET in regular trading on November 17, after Nvidia's quarterly holdings disclosure revealed a larger stake in the rocket and satellite company. Nvidia added 7.7 million shares in the third quarter, taking its position to 130.5 million. SpaceX now outranks Intel as the chipmaker's biggest disclosed equity bet.

The position was worth about $19.7 billion at September 30, or roughly $151 a share. Appaloosa Management built a bigger bet as well, buying 3,658,329 shares to reach 3,883,329 shares valued at about $556.6 million. The fund held only 225,000 shares at the end of June.

At today's price Nvidia's stake is worth about $18.3 billion, roughly 7% below the September 30 mark, and it equals less than 1% of SpaceX's $1.91 trillion market value. That makes the purchase a sign of strategic alignment, not a valuation floor. GuruFocus gives SpaceX a GF Score of just 21/100, dragged down by weak profitability, so investors are paying for future launch and Starlink growth rather than current returns. The next hurdle is quarterly results that show earnings catching up with a valuation already in the trillion-dollar club.

title: SpaceX Stocks Rise 2.63% as Nvidia Makes It Its Largest Disclosed Holding
